productDescription: A habit tracker for runners that turns a running goal into a daily streak. It logs each run, shows the current and longest streak, and nudges the runner before a streak is about to break. The point is consistency, not pace analytics.

personas.name: The Consistency Seeker
personas.trigger: Has tried and abandoned a running routine at least twice and wants a habit that finally sticks.
exclusions: Not a competitive racer chasing a PR
Not a data scientist who wants deep pace and cadence analytics
jobs: See at a glance whether today's run is done
Feel the pull of an unbroken streak
Get a reminder before the streak is at risk

scenarios.context: Just finished a 5am run before work
scenarios.goal: Log the run in under ten seconds and watch the streak count go up
scenarios.successSignal: Median time from opening the app to a logged run is under 10 seconds

scenarios.context: It is 8pm and no run has been logged today
scenarios.goal: Get a nudge in time to either run or consciously use a rest day
scenarios.successSignal: At least 60 percent of at-risk streaks receive a same-day reminder that is acted on

needs.title: Log a run with a single tap
needs.description: The core loop must be effortless or the habit never forms.

ears.ears: WHEN the runner taps the primary Log Run control on the Today screen, THE SYSTEM SHALL record a run for the current day and increment the streak within one second.
WHEN a run has already been logged for the current day, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the day as complete and SHALL NOT create a duplicate entry.

needs.title: Make the streak the emotional centerpiece
needs.description: The current and longest streak must be the first thing the runner sees.

ears.ears: WHEN the Today screen is opened, THE SYSTEM SHALL display the current streak length and the longest streak length above the fold.

needs.title: Warn before a streak breaks
needs.description: A missed day silently breaks the streak unless the runner is nudged.

ears.ears: WHEN no run has been logged and the runner's configured reminder time is reached, THE SYSTEM SHALL send a local notification warning that the streak is at risk.

features.title: One-tap Today logging
features.description: A single large primary action on the Today screen that logs the day's run.
acceptanceCriteria: Primary action is reachable without scrolling
Logging is idempotent per calendar day

ears.ears: WHEN the runner logs a run, THE SYSTEM SHALL persist it locally so the streak survives an app restart with no network.

features.title: Streak engine
features.description: Computes current streak, longest streak, and at-risk status from the run log.
acceptanceCriteria: A logged rest day does not break the streak

features.title: At-risk local reminder
features.description: Schedules a same-day local notification when the streak is unlogged near the reminder time.
acceptanceCriteria: Reminder is cancelled once the day is logged

uxFlows.name: Log a run and see the streak grow
steps: Open the app to the Today screen
See the streak counter animate upward
Optionally open the Streak History screen to see the calendar

screens.name: Today
screens.purpose: The home base: shows today's status, the current streak, and the one-tap Log Run action.

screens.name: Streak History
screens.purpose: A month calendar showing logged, rest, and missed days plus the longest-streak marker.

dataPoints.name: RunEntry
dataPoints.description: One logged run: the calendar date, whether it was a rest day, and the created timestamp.

dataPoints.name: RunStartLocation
dataPoints.description: Optional coarse start location attached to a run when the runner opts in to map view.
dataPoints.handlingNote: Stored on-device only, never synced to a server, and coarsened to city-block granularity. Deleted with the run entry.

integrations.name: Apple HealthKit
integrations.purpose: Read workout samples so a run recorded by another app can auto-complete today's streak.
codeSetup: Enable the HealthKit capability for the app target.
Add a user-facing NSHealthShareUsageDescription value for workout-read access.

externalManualActions.surface: iOS Health access permission prompt on a physical test device
externalManualActions.action: Grant the app read access to workout data when the system prompt appears.
externalManualActions.verification: Open Health Settings, confirm workout read access is enabled for StrideStreak, then import a sample workout.

verification: With read access granted and a sample workout present, verify that the workout is detected and today's streak updates once.
With access denied, verify that manual run logging remains available and no workout data is read.

apiContracts.description: Optional cloud backup of the local run log for a signed-in runner. Off by default.
apiContracts.requestSchema: { deviceId: string, entries: Array<{ date: string, restDay: boolean }> }
apiContracts.responseSchema: { currentStreak: number, longestStreak: number, syncedAt: string }

tests.description: Logging the same calendar day twice increments the streak only once and creates no duplicate RunEntry.
A granted workout is imported exactly once, while denied HealthKit access preserves manual run logging.
An at-risk reminder fires once at the configured time and is cancelled after the day is logged.
The history screen renders empty, loaded, and month-navigation states from persisted run entries.

adrs.title: Local-first storage with optional cloud sync
adrs.context: Runners log daily, often offline mid-run, and are privacy-sensitive about location data.
adrs.decision: Persist the run log on-device with SwiftData as the source of truth; cloud sync is opt-in and additive.
adrs.consequences: Streaks work fully offline and no account is required. The tradeoff is that cross-device continuity requires the opt-in sync path, and conflict resolution logic is deferred until sync ships.

assumptions.text: Runners think of a streak in whole calendar days, not rolling 24-hour windows.

risks.text: Too-frequent at-risk reminders train runners to ignore all notifications
risks.mitigation: Cap at one reminder per day and let the runner set the reminder time.

nonGoals.text: No pace, cadence, heart-rate, or route analytics in v1
nonGoals.because: The product's job is consistency, and analytics dashboards compete for attention with the single streak signal that drives the habit.

goals.statement: Make logging a run so fast it never becomes the reason a streak breaks.
Make the streak the emotional centerpiece that pulls the runner back daily.
goals.metric: Day-7 retention above 40 percent for runners with an active streak

goals.statement: Save at-risk streaks with a timely, non-nagging nudge before the day ends.

successMetrics.metric: Median time from opening the app to a logged run
Share of at-risk streaks that receive a same-day reminder acted on
Day-7 retention for runners who started a streak

slis.target: Time from Log Run tap to persisted entry
Share of at-risk days that fire a scheduled reminder

slos.target: at least 99 percent of scheduled reminders fire

always: Keep the run log usable fully offline
Keep location data on-device unless the runner explicitly opts into sync
askFirst: Before enabling cloud sync of the run log
Before requesting HealthKit or location permissions
never: Never sell or share run or location data with third parties
Never break an existing streak due to a background sync error

principles: Short and glanceable — the runner is often mid-stride

evidence.statement: The current app stores run entries locally and works without an account.
The streak remains the visual and emotional centerpiece.

accessibilityFloor: Use at least 44 by 44 point touch targets
mustAvoid: Dense pace analytics in the primary flow
